operators.description: Scan all 15M orders rows. For each row, evaluate NOT LIKE '%special%requests%' on o_comment. For passing rows, increment thread-local count_array[o_custkey]. This fuses the residual filter, LEFT JOIN probe, and first GROUP BY into a single pass.
operators.predicate_notes: Two-substring search: find 'special' then find 'requests' after it. Use strstr or memmem. Negate match. Estimated selectivity ~0.97 (only ~3% of comments match the pattern).

operators.description: Element-wise sum of all thread-local count arrays into a single global count_array[1500000]. Use SIMD vectorized addition.

Sweep merged_count_array for all valid custkeys (0..1499999). For each custkey, read c_count = merged_count_array[custkey]. Increment histogram[c_count]++. Customers with 0 matching orders get c_count=0 (the LEFT JOIN semantics — they appear with count 0). Use hash_customer_by_custkey to confirm valid custkey range (dense PK: all keys 0..1499999 are valid).
operators.notes: Max c_count per customer is bounded by max orders per customer (~40 at SF10). Allocate histogram[0..63] or dynamically sized.

operators.description: Convert non-zero histogram entries to (c_count, custdist) tuples. Sort by custdist DESC, c_count DESC.
operators.notes: Result set is tiny (~40 rows). std::sort is sufficient.

data_structures.per_thread_count_array: direct_array<uint16_t>[1500000] — one per thread, indexed by o_custkey

parallelism.notes: Step 1 is the bottleneck (15M rows with varlen o_comment access). Partition orders rows into morsels of 64K rows. Each thread maintains its own count_array to avoid contention. Step 2 merge is parallel across array segments. Steps 3-4 are single-threaded (trivially fast on 1.5M and ~40 entries respectively).

indexes.notes: Sequential scan of shared scan_orders_full is preferred over index-based random access since all orders must be examined for the o_comment filter.

memory_estimate_mb.notes: Fits comfortably in 376GB RAM. Per-thread arrays fit in L3 cache (44MB) when threads < 14.

left_join_semantics: Implicit via direct_array initialization to 0. All valid custkeys (0..1499999) are swept in step 3. Customers with no qualifying orders have count_array[custkey]=0, yielding c_count=0 — equivalent to LEFT JOIN producing NULLs that COUNT(o_orderkey) maps to 0.
